problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows the snapshot write failure in an empty catch with no comment, then unconditionally returns { ok: true, path, summary }. This is exactly the error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1 BAD shape (write failed, caller told it succeeded); the function's own doc promises the caller never ships a snapshot it believes holds the providers, yet a failed write yields the same success result as a good one.
impact: Trigger: writeOwnerOnlyFileAtomic throws (unwritable destPath, full disk, missing parent dir). Outcome: syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true) in loadOrRefreshWith reports a summary as if the pin was refreshed and any export caller prints success with a path that holds nothing or an old snapshot; the operator later goes offline relying on a pin that was never written. Class scope: the only catch in the new export path; the other new catch (removeProviderCatalogEntry) is commented best-effort and returns void, so it is not this shape. Enumerated by reading every catch the diff adds (3: snapshot.ts:74, snapshot.ts:95, cache.ts:263).

problem: A snapshot whose catalog.providers is missing or not an object is silently treated as an empty provider map ({}) instead of being refused like the other malformed shapes just above it (not an object, bad version, no catalog all throw). The failure is signalled by an empty collection the caller reads as a valid, empty snapshot (error-handling.mdc Rule 1 / Iron Law 2).
impact: Trigger: importProviderCatalogSnapshot(path, { prune: true }) on a hand-edited or truncated snapshot like {"version":1,"catalog":{}}. Outcome: nothing is imported, then the prune loop removes every cached provider and the result reports "0 provider(s), 0 live" as a successful import, wiping the operator's catalog. Without prune it still reports success for a file that carried no data. Class scope: single site; the other shape checks in this function (lines 99, 103, 107) all throw.

problem: The import doc comment states that a cache entry newer than the snapshot's copy is kept and only older or missing entries are replaced, but no code path does that: the loop calls updateProviderCatalogEntry unconditionally, and updateProviderCatalogEntry (provider-catalog-cache.ts:234) overwrites the entry by name with no fetchedAt comparison. The comment describes a behaviour that does not exist (lens C1a).
impact: A caller or reviewer trusting the doc will import an old pinned snapshot over a fresher cache expecting it to be a no-op for newer entries; the next maintainer reading the doc cannot tell which is intended. Fix the doc or add the comparison (the behavioural consequence belongs to the logic review).

An entry already in the cache that is newer than the snapshot's copy

problem: The JSON.parse catch both logs to stderr and rethrows the same error (error-handling.mdc Rule 5), and the rethrow is the raw SyntaxError with no context: every other failure in this function throws a contextual 'provider catalog snapshot: <path> ...' Error, but this one carries the path only in the stderr line, not in the error, and has no { cause } wrapping.
impact: Callers that report the error (e.g. loadOrRefreshWith via syncPinnedSnapshot) print an unlabelled 'Unexpected token' message, while the context appears separately on stderr, possibly twice once the caller logs. Wrap it: throw new Error(`provider catalog snapshot: ${srcPath} is not valid JSON`, { cause: e }) and drop the stderr write.

problem: The pinned-snapshot mirror is wired into loadOrRefreshWith with a different failure posture than every other cache write it sits beside: saveProviderCatalogCache and clearProviderCatalogCache are documented best-effort and never throw, but syncPinnedSnapshot can throw (export throws when the cache is absent, e.g. after a save that silently failed; import throws on an unreadable, non-JSON or wrong-version pin). The new code neither catches nor documents which posture applies.
impact: A courtesy side-copy can now fail the refresh call that just succeeded, contrary to the module's stated rule that a cache write never breaks the caller. Either catch at the call site with a comment giving the fallback, or document that pinning failures are surfaced on purpose.

impact: The parse/validate half cannot be tested or reused (e.g. by a 'snapshot verify' command) without performing cache writes. Extract parseProviderCatalogSnapshot(srcPath): ProviderCatalogSnapshot and keep the import as the merge step.
